During the battle, Felix traces the tower's mass bindings to the Girded Vow. The Star severs his left arm and leg, yet he destroys the oath anchor, frees Elowen, and redirects the weapon into the Tower Master. The tower begins collapsing as Felix escapes with Elowen. At the same time, Harn's force reaches the Poison Fields, where living prisoners are being used to refine ingredients for essence draughts.

Beef attacks the Overlord's adamant riders, protects escaping prisoners, and deploys armored risen across the Poison Fields. Harn, Kevin, and Shadow break through the manor defenses and kill Cade at the tower approach. Inside, they discover captives sealed in refinement jars while the Overlord, empowered as a divine vessel, turns their suffering into essence-draught ingredients. Archie phases prisoners out of the jars. Kevin and Shadow combine into the four-armed Dragomir, and Harn accepts Felix's distant boon, evolving several skills. Together they bind the Overlord and collapse the tower onto him. His divine protection fails, killing him and ending the refinement regime. The surviving captives are evacuated, although some prisoners die during the wider battle. Beef's risen hatchling survives an apparent death and returns in a stronger form. The Poison Fields operation has succeeded, leaving local recovery and government unresolved. In Sunara, Pit begins the Tempest trial rather than wait for Euphonia's leaders. He evades ancient storm wardens, gains help from elemental sprites, and reaches the calm center of the storm.

The Tempest recognizes Pit and grants him greater authority. At Halcyon Hold, he meets the Sylphan princess and her blind Corva guardian, whose visions support evacuation. A goddess immediately finds the refuge and corrupts Sunara's storm wardens. The guardian stays behind to delay the shadow beasts while Vessilia's fleet and Euphonia's defenders join the battle. Pit restores the damaged seal, claims authority over Sunara as Storm Tyrant, and helps the princess tear divine influence from the storm. Sunlight returns, but Imara appears and abducts the exhausted princess. Imara then attacks the survivors of the Poison Fields battle and takes Kevin and Shadow despite Archie's attempt to stop her. In Levantier, Felix survives with regenerated limbs and reaches Master Tier. Elowen wakes free of the oath network and explains the silver influence behind her work. Felix cannot destroy the Thonic Star, whose purpose is to find and break bindings. The devastated Violet Tower's mages are free, but the Star remains intact. Felix's armored sister then arrives, bringing the conflict with the goddess directly to him.

The goddess of fortune acts through Gabby, escapes with the Thonic Star, and turns nearby soldiers against Felix. He reopens her rift, drags much of the goddess into his reach, and drops the battle into Levantier's mana well when he cannot free the possessed soldiers. There a primordial remnant limits them both. Felix survives the flesh curse, completes several Grandmaster temperings, and receives the remnant's remaining dominion. He reclaims ancient oaths from the goddess, breaks her chains, evolves into a stronger primordial bloodline, and kills her. The silver moon vanishes, but the resulting experience is consumed by an unstable advancement that leaves Felix's level unreadable. He saves the falling city, then learns that Gabby covertly signaled her restored identity. At the Tower of True Faith, she has delivered the Thonic Star, the Sylphan princess, Kevin, and Shadow to the Hierophant while concealing her recovered will. The gods demand one final Unbound captive. Felix knows the captives' destination, but his transformation releases a cardinal beast from his shadow, forcing his allies to flee from the immediate danger.

characters.description: Queen of Terrasen in name, camped on her own southern border with a court of five and no army. She holds two of the three Wyrdkeys and a plan she will not share with anyone, including the people who have sworn their lives to her. She is running out of time, money, and allies at the same rate, and she has begun making trades whose full price she keeps to herself.
characters.name: Aelin Ashryver Galathynius

characters.description: A Fae prince of Doranelle, blood-sworn to Aelin and her closest confidant, with wind and ice magic and a hawk's form. He has stopped trying to talk her out of things and started making sure she survives them. He is the only person who reliably knows when she is lying.
characters.name: Rowan Whitethorn

characters.description: General of the Bane and Aelin's cousin, half Fae, blood-sworn to her and responsible for holding together the only fighting force loyal to her. He is furious with the Terrasen lords who will not acknowledge his queen, and openly hostile to the two Fae warriors Maeve has sent to shadow them.
characters.name: Aedion Ashryver

characters.description: A shapeshifter, formerly a courtesan of Rifthold, whose magic returned when the towers fell and who can now take any form she has studied. She is learning to fight, raising her ward Evangeline, and has made herself indispensable to Aelin as a scout, a spy, and a friend who is not afraid of her.
characters.name: Lysandra

characters.description: Lysandra's young ward, a scarred girl determined to be useful and increasingly aware of how dangerous the company she keeps has become.
characters.name: Evangeline

characters.description: The daughter of Terrasen's Lady of Perranth, on the road north out of Morath with a ruined ankle, a Wyrdstone shard, and orders from a dying woman to find Aelin Galathynius. She was raised locked in a tower and has almost no experience of the world, which she compensates for with patience and a very good ear for a lie.
characters.name: Elide Lochan

characters.description: A Fae warrior five centuries old, the most lethal of Queen Maeve's blood-sworn cadre, with dark magic that can smother life outright. Exiled and hunting the Wyrdkeys for his queen, he falls in with Elide on the road under a false name and finds himself escorting her north. He is loyal to Maeve above every other consideration.
characters.name: Lorcan Salvaterre

characters.description: Wing Leader of the Ironteeth host, sent out with the Thirteen to hunt Aelin Galathynius for Morath. She has begun asking questions her grandmother will not answer, chiefly about her own mother, and she is no longer certain the Ironteeth are on the right side of anything.
characters.name: Manon Blackbeak

characters.description: Manon's Second and cousin, the finest rider in the Thirteen, carrying a hundred years of a secret the Blackbeaks punished her for and have never let her speak of.
characters.name: Asterin Blackbeak

characters.description: The scarred runt wyvern Manon claimed, now the fastest flier in the host, who likes flowers, sunlight, and Manon, in roughly that order.
characters.name: Abraxos

characters.description: King of Adarlan, inheritor of his father's ruined empire and of magic he is still learning to use. He has lost his capital and most of his court and is trying to work out what one king with raw power and no army can actually do against Morath.
characters.name: Dorian Havilliard

characters.description: The senior lord of Terrasen's council, elderly and unsentimental, who kept the kingdom's remnants alive through ten years of occupation. He does not accept Aelin's claim: to him she is a girl who vanished, spent a decade as an assassin for hire, and has come back with no army, no treasury, and no proof she can rule.
characters.name: Lord Darrow

characters.description: Matron of the Blackbeak clan and Manon's grandmother, who has commanded the Ironteeth for five centuries and intends to lead them back into their stolen kingdom in the west whatever the cost to her own bloodline.
characters.name: The Blackbeak Matron

characters.description: A Fae warrior of Maeve's cadre, young by Fae reckoning, with a wolf's form and a twin brother he does not talk about. He is charming, insolent, and bound by a blood oath he plainly resents, sent along with Gavriel to watch Aelin and report back.
characters.name: Fenrys

characters.description: A Fae warrior of Maeve's cadre known as the Lion, quiet and courteous, with a mountain lion's form. He fought in Terrasen decades ago, and Aedion Ashryver is his son, a fact neither of them has any idea what to do with.
characters.name: Gavriel

characters.description: Pirate Lord of Skull's Bay in the Dead Islands, whose hands carry a magical map of the seas. He and Aelin have unfinished business from years ago, and he has spent the time since building a fleet and an empire of his own out of the Bay.
characters.name: Captain Rolfe

characters.description: The first Queen of Adarlan, a thousand years dead, who has steered Aelin's life from the beginning. She finally begins explaining what she has been building toward, the gate, the keys, and the Lock, and what it will cost the person who closes it.
characters.name: Elena Galathynius

characters.description: The Valg king who was defeated a thousand years ago and never destroyed, now awake at Morath and in command of its armies, its ilken, and its Wyrdstone. He holds the third key and wants the other two.
characters.name: Erawan

characters.description: Queen of the Fae of Doranelle, Aelin's great-aunt, who was denied Aelin's blood oath and lost Rowan to her. She has been patient about it. Her cadre is scattered across the continent on errands she has not explained, and her fleet is not where anyone expected it to be.
characters.name: Maeve

recaps.ending: The book ends with Aelin in chains. At the coast, with the ritual to forge the Lock finally within reach, Maeve arrives with a fleet, having been told exactly where to find her by Lorcan. Aelin surrenders herself to spare her court and her allies, and Maeve has her beaten, bound in iron, and sealed inside an iron coffin, taking her away by ship along with Fenrys, whose blood oath forces him to go. Rowan, Aedion, Lysandra, Elide, and Gavriel are left alive on the shore with nothing but the promise to find her. Lorcan is exiled from the court for the betrayal, with Elide the one who names the sentence. It emerges that Aelin had prepared for a version of this: Lysandra will wear her face and hold Terrasen together, buying the kingdom time it does not know it needs. Manon Blackbeak survives her grandmother's attempt to kill her and learns that she is the daughter of the last Crochan Queen, half of the people the Ironteeth have hunted for five hundred years; she and the Thirteen become outcasts and turn west to find the Crochans and, if they will have her, a crown. Dorian is left carrying the war on the northern front with a witch's help and no plan. Erawan holds Morath, one Wyrdkey, and an army nobody has yet slowed down.
recaps.in_short: Refused recognition by Terrasen's lords, Aelin gambles everything on alliances she cannot pay for: she wins Rolfe's pirate fleet at Skull's Bay by destroying a Valg armada, courts the sea dragons and the Fae, and marries Rowan. Elide Lochan travels north with Lorcan Salvaterre, Maeve's exiled warrior, carrying a Wyrdstone shard toward a queen she has never met. Dorian, driven out of a fallen Rifthold, falls in with the witch Manon Blackbeak, and the two raid the Ferian Gap and turn toward Morath after the third Wyrdkey. Manon's defiance finally provokes her grandmother, who tries to kill her and reveals that Manon is the daughter of the last Crochan Queen; Manon and the Thirteen break with the Ironteeth. Aelin learns from Elena the true price of forging the Lock and closing the Wyrdgate: her own life. She spends the book concealing that from everyone. At the coast, on the verge of the ritual, Lorcan's message brings Maeve's fleet down on them. Aelin gives herself up to save her court, and is chained in iron and shipped away in a coffin, leaving Rowan and the others to find her and Lysandra to wear her face.

recaps.text: Previously: Aelin Galathynius returned to Rifthold, freed her condemned cousin Aedion, and took back her old life on her own terms, killing the assassin master Arobynn Hamel and inheriting his fortune along with the Amulet of Orynth, which proved to contain the third Wyrdkey. Lysandra, a courtesan of the city, was revealed as a shapeshifter and became her ally. Aelin destroyed the black tower that had kept magic dead for a decade, restoring it across the continent, then confronted the king of Adarlan; Dorian Havilliard broke the Valg collar on his own will and killed his father, who claimed with his last breath that he too had been a Valg puppet. The blast that ended it shattered Chaol Westfall's spine, and he sailed for the southern continent with Nesryn Faliq to seek healing and an army. Aelin brought down the glass castle and left Dorian a king over ruins. At Morath, the witch Manon Blackbeak defied her clan to free a servant named Elide Lochan, and the dying Kaltain Rompier destroyed much of the fortress, pressing a Wyrdstone shard into Elide's hand and telling her to find Celaena Sardothien. Behind it all stood Erawan, the Valg king, awake and unopposed at Morath. Aelin turned north for Terrasen with two of the three keys and no army.

Aelin reaches Terrasen's border and is met not with a crown but with a summons. Lord Darrow, who held the kingdom's remnants together through the occupation, refuses to recognize her: she has no army, no treasury, and a decade of assassin's work behind her, and he tells her plainly that she will not be queen. Her whole court is five people. Aedion is incandescent, Rowan is calculating, and Aelin turns south instead, chasing money and ships rather than legitimacy. Elide Lochan, meanwhile, is walking north out of Morath with a shattered ankle and Kaltain's Wyrdstone shard sewn into her clothes, and falls in with a hard, unfriendly man calling himself Lorcan, who is in fact Lorcan Salvaterre, Maeve's most dangerous warrior, hunting the Wyrdkeys for his queen. Neither tells the other the truth. In the north, Manon Blackbeak is ordered to hunt Aelin down, and finds herself stalling. Erawan's forces move out of Morath in numbers, and Rifthold falls, driving Dorian out of his own capital.

Two of Maeve's cadre, Fenrys and Gavriel, catch up with Aelin's party and attach themselves to it under orders to observe. Aedion realizes that the courteous, quiet Gavriel is his father, a fact neither of them handles well. Aelin sets course for Skull's Bay in the Dead Islands to buy or bully a fleet out of the Pirate Lord Rolfe, with whom she has old and unpleasant history. Lysandra practises new shapes and begins working as Aelin's scout. Elide and Lorcan continue north, hunted by ilken, Erawan's winged creations, and their partnership becomes something neither will name. Manon's grandmother grows suspicious of her hesitation and starts testing her. Dorian, homeless and hunted, works his way north with magic he can barely aim, and the war reaches the coastal towns before any of the kingdoms are ready for it.

At Skull's Bay, Aelin takes over Rolfe's town by simply installing herself in it, and their negotiation is interrupted by the war arriving: a Valg fleet enters the bay, escorted by things that are not men. Aelin and Rowan destroy it, and the sea dragons of legend rise to help. Rolfe, whose enchanted map has begun showing him what is coming, throws in with her, and the old Mycenian alliance is revived; Aelin now has ships. She also has a reputation spreading ahead of her as the Fire-Bringer. In the north, Dorian and Manon Blackbeak meet, and after an initial standoff decide they are more useful to each other than to anyone else. Elide and Lorcan reach the fringes of the war and are drawn toward Aelin's path. Manon's defiance is now open enough that the Blackbeak Matron begins arranging an answer to it.

Elena's spirit finally tells Aelin what has been withheld from her since the first tomb: the gate between worlds cannot simply be locked with the keys returned to it. A new Lock must be forged, and forging it will consume the person who does it. Aelin has been told, in effect, that the plan she has organized her life around ends with her death, and she keeps it from Rowan, from Aedion, from all of them, while quietly making arrangements for what comes after. She continues gathering allies, ships, and leverage, and begins spending money and promises at a rate her court finds alarming. Dorian and Manon travel together toward the Ferian Gap, where Erawan keeps wyverns and, they believe, the last Wyrdkey may be traced. Elide and Lorcan, still lying to each other about who they are, arrive close enough to Aelin's forces to be noticed.

Dorian and Manon strike the Ferian Gap, destroying part of Erawan's breeding operation, and their alliance turns into something more complicated for both of them. Aelin and Rowan stop pretending about what they are to each other and acknowledge the bond between them openly. Aelin also begins building the trap she means to spring on Erawan, a plan that requires her to be exactly where he expects her to be, and continues spending money, ships, and promises at a rate that alarms her own court. Elide and Lorcan, still each concealing who they really are, work their way closer to Aelin's forces through country the war has already crossed. Manon is summoned by her grandmother and goes knowing it is a reckoning rather than an audience, and the Thirteen go with her.

The Blackbeak Matron tries to have Manon killed, and in doing so reveals what has been hidden from her for a century: Manon is the daughter of Rhiannon Crochan, the last Crochan Queen, whom the Matron murdered. Manon is half of the people the Ironteeth have hunted for five hundred years, and she was bred as a weapon against them. The Thirteen fight their way out, and Manon, gravely wounded, is carried away by Abraxos; her coven are outcasts now, hunted by every Ironteeth clan, and she turns west toward the Wastes to look for the Crochans she was raised to exterminate. Elide finally reaches Aelin and delivers Kaltain's Wyrdstone shard, and the truth about Lorcan comes out on all sides: he has been Maeve's the whole time. Elide is taken into Aelin's court and promised Perranth. Aelin and Rowan are wed, quickly and without ceremony, in the middle of a war. The fleet and the allies gather on the southern coast for the ritual that will forge the Lock. Lorcan, cast out of the group's trust and convinced he is protecting his queen's interests, sends word to Maeve about exactly where Aelin will be.

Maeve's fleet arrives at the coast in overwhelming force. With her court outnumbered and her allies about to be slaughtered, Aelin makes the trade: herself for their lives. Maeve takes her, beaten and chained in iron, and seals her in an iron coffin aboard ship, and Fenrys, bound by blood oath, is compelled to go with them. Rowan, Aedion, Lysandra, Elide, and Gavriel are left standing on the shore. Lorcan's betrayal is exposed, and Elide casts him out of the court herself. What Aelin left behind is a contingency: Lysandra will take her shape and hold Terrasen together while the rest of them hunt for her, and only a handful of people will know the queen at Orynth is not the queen. Manon, cast out and half dead, rides west to find the Crochans with the Thirteen. Dorian carries on north with what he has learned about the third key. Erawan still holds Morath, his armies are moving, and the one person who could close the gate is in a box on the sea.

characters.description: A brilliant, deeply empathetic six-year-old boy, the rare third child in a family in a future where population law allows only two. He was permitted to be born because the military hopes he will become the commander who can save humanity from a feared third alien invasion. He combines an unusual capacity to understand others with a willingness to answer a threat with total, decisive force when he believes he has no choice, a combination that both his teachers and his enemies exploit.
characters.name: Ender Wiggin

characters.description: The officer in charge of Battle School, who selects Ender and takes personal responsibility for shaping him. Convinced that humanity's survival depends on producing one great commander, he deliberately isolates Ender and keeps him under constant pressure, willing to be cruel and to make himself the boy's enemy if that is what forging a leader requires.
characters.name: Colonel Graff

characters.description: Ender's older brother, as gifted as anyone in the family but cruel and domineering, rejected by the military for being too ruthless. He torments Ender and their sister and is driven by a hunger for power and control.
characters.name: Peter Wiggin

characters.description: Ender's older sister, as intelligent as her brothers but gentle and compassionate, and fiercely protective of Ender. She was passed over by the military for being too soft, and she is the person Ender loves and misses most once he is taken away.
characters.name: Valentine Wiggin

characters.description: A capable boy among the young recruits at Battle School who becomes a genuine friend to Ender, joining his extra practice sessions and offering him rare warmth and loyalty in an environment designed to keep him alone.
characters.name: Alai

characters.description: The proud, hot-tempered commander of Salamander Army, the unit Ender is assigned to while still very young. Jealous of Ender's talent and obsessed with his own honor, he refuses to let Ender fight in the battle-room games and comes to hate him.
characters.name: Bonzo Madrid

characters.description: One of the few girls at Battle School and a top soldier in Salamander Army. Defying her commander, she befriends Ender and secretly trains him as a marksman, becoming an early ally and one of the students he trusts.
characters.name: Petra Arkanian

characters.description: A respected older soldier and leader in Rat Army who mentors Ender and speaks openly about his doubts, suggesting that the teachers may be manipulating all of them and that the coming war may not be what the children have been told.
characters.name: Dink Meeker

characters.description: A very small, exceptionally clever young recruit placed in the army Ender is given to command. Ender recognizes in Bean the same isolation and promise that the teachers once saw in himself, and singles him out for hard treatment and greater responsibility.
characters.name: Bean

characters.description: The legendary commander who saved humanity by destroying the alien fleet during the previous invasion, long believed dead. He reappears as Ender's stern and demanding final teacher at Command School, drilling him relentlessly for the war to come.
characters.name: Mazer Rackham

characters.description: An insectlike alien species governed by hive queens whose two earlier invasions nearly destroyed humanity. The dread of a third invasion is the reason Earth's governments train gifted children like Ender to lead the coming war, and defeating the buggers is the purpose behind everything the schools do.
characters.name: The Buggers

recaps.ending: Ender's final training exercise turns out to have been the real war: unknowingly commanding actual human fleets he believed were only simulations, he fires a planet-destroying weapon at the buggers' homeworld, annihilating their entire species. The adults had concealed the truth so that he would fight without the moral weight of committing genocide. Ender is left shattered by what he was tricked into doing. On Earth, the alliance that fought the aliens fractures into war, and his brother Peter, working through politics and propaganda, rises toward ruling the world. Refusing to be used again or to go home, Ender leaves with his sister Valentine to help colonize one of the buggers' abandoned worlds. There he discovers that the aliens had come to understand him and had preserved a single dormant hive queen, leaving her in his care along with a plea for their revival. Ender accepts the burden of carrying the queen egg to find her a new home one day, and he writes a book told from the aliens' point of view that recasts them as victims rather than monsters. Under the name Speaker for the Dead, he begins a life of atonement, leaving open the possibility of the buggers' eventual return.
recaps.in_short: In a future still recovering from two invasions by an insectlike alien species, the world's military trains brilliant children to command the war against a feared third attack. Six-year-old Ender Wiggin, chosen for his rare mix of empathy and ruthlessness, is taken to an orbiting Battle School, where Colonel Graff deliberately isolates him to forge him into a leader. Ender rises through the school's zero-gravity war games, enduring bullying, manipulation, and crushing pressure, and eventually commands his own army with unmatched skill, though the strain nearly breaks him. Promoted to Command School, he is trained by Mazer Rackham, the hero of the last war, and directs entire fleets through grueling battle simulations. In a final test against overwhelming odds, Ender destroys the enemy's home planet, only to learn afterward that the simulations were real and that he has wiped out the entire alien species. Devastated by the deception, he refuses to return to Earth and leaves to help settle a new world, where he discovers the aliens were not the monsters humanity believed and dedicates himself to honoring the dead.

recaps.text: In a future where humanity has barely survived two invasions by an insectlike alien species called the buggers, the world government trains gifted children to become military commanders for an expected third war. Andrew, called Ender, Wiggin is a brilliant, empathetic six-year-old, a rare third child in a family limited by law to two, watched since birth as a candidate. After the monitoring device implanted at his neck is removed, a school bully corners him and Ender responds with overwhelming force to make sure the threat can never return. At home he is caught between his loving sister, Valentine, and his cruel, power-hungry brother, Peter. Colonel Graff, an officer of Battle School, recruits Ender and takes him away to an orbiting military academy, at once beginning to isolate him from the other recruits so that he learns to depend only on himself.

At Battle School, Ender endures Graff's deliberate manipulation, which turns the other students against him. He masters the school's central exercise, mock battles fought with freeze weapons in a weightless arena, quickly outthinking older students with unconventional tactics. In his free time he is drawn into a strange computer fantasy game that seems to adapt itself to his mind, and he forces his way past one of its supposedly unbeatable challenges through sheer stubbornness. Despite his isolation he begins forming real bonds, notably with a boy named Alai, and he organizes extra practice sessions to sharpen his own skills and those of the recruits who follow him.

The teachers accelerate Ender's training, promoting him early into Salamander Army under the resentful commander Bonzo Madrid, who forbids him to fight; a skilled soldier named Petra secretly trains him instead. Reassigned soon after to Rat Army, Ender keeps mentoring younger students in private practice and hears older soldiers like Dink Meeker voice suspicion that the adults are manipulating them all. Meanwhile, back on Earth, his siblings Peter and Valentine secretly build political influence under false identities on the world's computer networks, with Peter aiming to seize real power. Ender's steady, brilliant success leads the teachers to hand him command of his own newly formed army.

Ender is given command of Dragon Army, assembled from castoffs and very young recruits, among them a gifted small boy named Bean. He trains them with inventive tactics and leads them to victory after victory as the teachers rig the games against him, forcing battles under increasingly unfair conditions to test his limits. The relentless schedule isolates and exhausts him. Bonzo Madrid's hatred finally boils over: he confronts Ender with a gang of boys, and Ender, fighting to survive, beats Bonzo so severely that the threat is ended for good, though he is not told the full outcome. Drained and disturbed by his own capacity for violence, Ender is pushed to the edge of collapse.

Worn down and frightened by what he is becoming, Ender is sent back to Earth for a rest, where the military quietly uses his sister Valentine to persuade him not to give up. He agrees to keep going and is sent far out in the solar system to Command School. There his teacher is Mazer Rackham, the legendary hero who destroyed the alien fleet in the previous war and was long believed dead. Mazer trains Ender to command entire fleets through a realistic battle simulator, with his old friends serving as his squadron leaders, driving him through brutal, exhausting practice engagements while telling him the real invasion is near.

For his final examination, Ender faces an impossible scenario: the enemy fleet vastly outnumbers his own around their home planet. He orders a forbidden weapon fired directly at the planet itself, destroying it along with the entire enemy fleet. Only afterward does Mazer reveal the truth: the exercises were never simulations but real battles fought by actual human fleets under Ender's command, and Ender has just wiped out the entire bugger species. Devastated to learn he committed genocide without knowing it, Ender falls into a long breakdown. On Earth, war erupts among the victorious nations and Peter maneuvers toward ruling the world. Ender refuses to go home; instead he travels with Valentine to help settle a former bugger world, where he discovers that the aliens were not the mindless enemy humanity believed. They left behind a dormant hive queen and a message meant for him, and he takes up her egg to one day revive her kind, writing a book of atonement that becomes the first work of the Speaker for the Dead.

characters.description: A girl born as the eighth child of a village blacksmith in the Ramtop mountains. By an accident of a dying wizard's gift she inherits a wizard's staff and a talent for magic. Because tradition divides magic strictly by sex, with men becoming wizards and women becoming witches, her wizardly ability is treated as impossible, and she grows up caught awkwardly between the two crafts.
characters.name: Eskarina Smith

characters.description: The witch of the village of Bad Ass, a stern and formidable older woman who trusts shrewd judgement, herb-lore, and sheer force of character more than flashy spells. She takes responsibility for Esk after the wizard's gift lands on the child, and sets out to teach her the disciplined, practical craft of witchcraft.
characters.name: Granny Weatherwax

characters.description: An elderly wizard nearing death who, following an old custom, seeks out the eighth son of an eighth son to receive his staff and power. He passes the gift to a newborn without confirming that the child is a boy, an oversight that sets the whole story in motion.
characters.name: Drum Billet

characters.description: The village blacksmith and Esk's father, a practical, down-to-earth man made uneasy by the strange magical inheritance that has fallen on his young daughter.
characters.name: Gordo Smith

characters.description: A witch in the market town of Ohulan Cutash whom Granny consults about Esk. More worldly and comfortable with town life than the mountain witches, she trades in charms and remedies.
characters.name: Hilta Goatfounder

characters.description: A wizard traveling through the mountains who meets Esk and Granny and reacts with blank disbelief at the notion that a girl could carry and use a wizard's staff.
characters.name: Treatle

characters.description: A frail young man with a severe stammer and an extraordinary gift for magical theory, studying at the wizards' Unseen University. His mind reaches insights far beyond those of his teachers, which makes him both remarkable and, without his knowing it, dangerous.
characters.name: Simon

characters.description: The Archchancellor of the Unseen University, senior among the wizards, who upholds the long-standing rule that only men may be admitted to study there. He becomes Granny Weatherwax's chief opponent, and unlikely counterpart, in the argument over Esk.
characters.name: Cutangle

recaps.ending: Simon's gift for magical theory grows so strong that it draws the attention of the Things from the Dungeon Dimensions, mindless entities that hunger to invade the world through the openings his thinking creates. When his magic pulls him into that cold, formless other place, Esk follows to bring him back, using her own staff and the connection between them. Granny Weatherwax reaches them by borrowing her way into the University and lending Esk her strength. Working together, Esk's instinctive witch craft and Simon's raw power drive the invaders back and close the breach. Both children survive, changed by the experience. The confrontation forces the wizards to recognize that the strict division of magic by sex is neither natural nor safe: Esk has done what no rule said she could. The story closes with the barrier between wizardry and witchcraft cracked open, Esk accepted as something new, and the way cleared for women to be taught at the University at last.
recaps.in_short: A dying wizard passes his staff and power to what he believes is the eighth son of an eighth son in a small mountain village, only for the newborn to be a girl, Eskarina Smith. Since custom holds that women can only be witches and men only wizards, Esk's wizardly gift is treated as impossible. The village witch, Granny Weatherwax, tries to raise her as a witch, but the wizard magic keeps breaking loose. Granny finally takes Esk to the Unseen University in Ankh-Morpork and demands she be admitted, only to be turned away because she is a girl. At the University Esk befriends Simon, a brilliant but sickly student whose powerful theoretical magic accidentally opens the way to the Dungeon Dimensions, letting alien creatures reach toward the world. Esk is drawn into that other realm to save him. Combining witch sense with wizard power, she and Granny pull Simon back and drive the creatures off. In the aftermath the rigid line between the two kinds of magic begins to soften, and the University edges toward admitting women.

recaps.text: In the Ramtop mountains of the Discworld, tradition holds that magic is divided by sex: men become wizards, trained at the Unseen University, while women become witches, working alone in their villages. A dying wizard named Drum Billet travels to the small village of Bad Ass to give his staff and power to the eighth son of an eighth son, as custom demands. He hands the gift to a newborn child, only to discover too late that the baby is a girl, Eskarina Smith. The village witch, Granny Weatherwax, foresees that this is going to cause trouble, because a girl with a wizard's staff is something the world is not supposed to allow. As Esk grows, her inherited magic begins to surface in ways that fit neither the witch's craft Granny knows nor anything the mountains have seen before.

characters.description: A fifteen-year-old farm boy raised by his uncle in Palancar Valley, near the isolated mountain village of Carvahall. While hunting in the forbidding range called the Spine, he finds a smooth blue stone that turns out to be a dragon egg. Curious, practical, and stubborn, he is thrust out of his ordinary life when the egg hatches and binds him to its dragon, making him a Dragon Rider, the first new one in a generation. He must learn quickly what that means while danger closes in on his home.
characters.name: Eragon

characters.description: The sapphire-blue dragon that hatches from the stone Eragon found, bonding to him mind to mind the moment he touches her. She grows with astonishing speed from a small hatchling into a powerful flying companion, sharing thoughts, emotions, and eventually speech with Eragon. Proud, fierce, and protective, she is both his closest friend and his partner in the ancient legacy of the Riders, and their two lives are now tied together for as long as they both live.
characters.name: Saphira

characters.description: The gruff old storyteller of Carvahall, known for reciting tales of the vanished Dragon Riders. He proves to know far more about dragons, magic, and the wider world than a village elder should. When disaster strikes Eragon's home, Brom sets out with him, becoming his traveling companion and demanding teacher in swordsmanship and the ancient language through which magic is worked. Secretive about his own past, he guides Eragon's first dangerous steps as a Rider.
characters.name: Brom

characters.description: Eragon's uncle, a hardworking and stern but caring farmer who raised him as his own son alongside his own boy, Roran. Plainspoken and proud of his self-reliance, he keeps the family's small holding outside Carvahall through hard seasons and expects honesty and effort from those in his care.
characters.name: Garrow

characters.description: Eragon's older cousin and closest thing to a brother, Garrow's son. Steady, strong, and level-headed, he plans to marry a local girl and make his own way, and near the start of the story leaves the farm to take paid work in a neighboring town. His fortunes and Eragon's will remain entwined.
characters.name: Roran

characters.description: A skilled young swordsman who appears suddenly to rescue Eragon from deadly pursuers and then travels with him. Well-armed, well-trained, and clearly raised to more than a common life, he is guarded and bitter about his origins and reluctant to speak of where he comes from or approach centers of power. Loyal in a fight but wary of trust, he carries the weight of a past he would rather leave behind.
characters.name: Murtagh

characters.description: An elf whom Eragon first glimpses in troubling dreams and then finds held prisoner and poisoned in an enemy fortress. Strong-willed, reserved, and dangerous, she was carrying the dragon egg when it was intercepted and is bound up in the struggle against the Empire. Gravely ill from her captivity, she needs to reach the rebels who can heal her, and she becomes a crucial link between Eragon and the wider war.
characters.name: Arya

characters.description: An eccentric herbalist and fortune-teller Eragon meets in the port city of Teirm. Sharp-tongued, witty, and unpredictable, she reads his future with carved bones and gives cryptic, unsettling prophecies. She keeps the company of a werecat and clearly knows more magic than she admits, though her true loyalties and depth remain a mystery.
characters.name: Angela

characters.description: The commanding, imposing leader of the Varden, the rebel force that shelters in the hidden dwarf stronghold beneath the mountains and works to overthrow the king. Disciplined and shrewd, he weighs whether the newly arrived young Rider is an asset or a risk to his cause, and he holds together an uneasy alliance of humans, dwarves, and elves against a far greater power.
characters.name: Ajihad

characters.description: Ajihad's poised and intelligent daughter, who moves capably within the Varden's leadership. Composed and quietly ambitious, she takes an early measure of Eragon and shows a talent for politics and command that hints at a larger role to come in the rebellion.
characters.name: Nasuada

characters.description: A Shade, a sorcerer whose body has been taken over by malevolent spirits, granting him terrible power and unnatural strength but a cruel, unstable nature. Serving the king, he leads the hunt for the dragon egg and its Rider, striking down any who stand in his way. Pale, red-haired, and merciless, he is among the deadliest servants of the Empire.
characters.name: Durza

characters.description: The tyrant king of the Empire, himself a former Dragon Rider who long ago betrayed and destroyed the old order of Riders to seize absolute power. Feared across the land, he has ruled for generations through fear, sorcery, and force. Though he does not appear directly, his hunt for the last dragon egg and its Rider drives the danger that pursues Eragon from the first.
characters.name: Galbatorix

recaps.ending: Eragon reaches the Varden's mountain stronghold of Farthen Dur, where Arya is healed and he meets their leader, Ajihad. An army of the king's monstrous Urgals soon assaults the fortress. In the vast battle underground, Eragon and Saphira face the Shade Durza, who wounds Eragon terribly across the back; distracted at the crucial moment, Durza is stabbed through the heart, and his death breaks the enemy's will and turns the tide. As Eragon recovers, a distant presence reaches into his mind: a teacher who calls himself the Cripple Who Is Whole, summoning him to the elven forest of Du Weldenvarden to finish learning what it means to be a Rider. Eragon has survived his first war, lost his mentor Brom, gained an uneasy friend in Murtagh, and glimpsed the scale of the fight against Galbatorix. He and Saphira prepare to leave for their training, their part in the rebellion only beginning.
recaps.in_short: Eragon, a farm boy in a remote valley, finds a blue stone that hatches into a dragon he names Saphira, making him the first new Dragon Rider in a generation. When the king's servants kill his uncle and burn his home hunting the dragon, Eragon flees with Brom, the village storyteller, who is secretly a former Rider and teaches him swordplay and magic as they pursue the killers. Brom dies in an ambush, and a mysterious young man, Murtagh, joins Eragon. Guided by visions, Eragon frees a captive elf, Arya, and races to deliver her to the Varden, the rebels opposing King Galbatorix, in their hidden dwarf city beneath the mountains. There an enemy army attacks, and in the battle Eragon confronts and destroys the Shade Durza, though he is badly wounded. Recovering, he is contacted mind to mind by a hidden teacher who summons him to the elves' forest to complete his training.

recaps.text: Eragon is a fifteen-year-old boy raised on a small farm outside the remote village of Carvahall by his uncle Garrow, alongside his older cousin Roran. While hunting in the wild mountains called the Spine, he finds a smooth blue stone. It later cracks open to reveal a dragon hatchling, which bonds to him and marks him as a Dragon Rider, one of an order thought long dead. Eragon hides the growing dragon in the woods, feeds and cares for her in secret, and names her Saphira. As their minds link and she grows swiftly, he begins to grasp that his quiet life is over and that possessing a dragon is dangerous knowledge in a land ruled by a king who once destroyed the Riders.

Two sinister strangers, servants of the king, come to Carvahall asking about the stone. Eragon and Saphira flee, but the pursuers find the farm, fatally wound Garrow, and burn the home. Grief-stricken and set on revenge, Eragon leaves the valley to hunt the killers. He is joined by Brom, the old village storyteller, who surprises him by knowing a great deal about dragons and magic and by insisting on coming along. As they travel, Brom trains Eragon in swordsmanship and in the ancient language through which spells are cast, and slowly reveals that his own past is bound up with the lost Riders. Eragon commits himself to mastering his new powers while chasing the ones responsible for his uncle's death.

Eragon and Brom follow the trail of the king's servants across the countryside, and Eragon's skills grow through hard practice and real danger. When they come upon a village destroyed by raiders, Eragon uses magic in earnest for the first time, and Brom teaches him more about its rules and costs. Along the way Eragon learns fragments of the wider world: the tyranny of King Galbatorix, the vanished glory of the Riders, and the shadowy rebels who resist the Empire. The pursuit leads them toward the coastal city of Teirm as they try to pick up the cold trail of their quarry and understand who truly hunts the last dragon and her Rider.

In the port city of Teirm, Brom seeks out an old friend named Jeod to gather information, and Eragon crosses paths with the eccentric herbalist Angela and her companion, a werecat, who give him strange and troubling prophecies about his future. Using records in the city, they trace the movements of their enemies and set off again, now aimed toward the dark city of Dras-Leona where the king's servants are thought to lurk. Eragon continues to train, tests his growing magic, and begins to feel the weight of being hunted, even as he presses on with Brom toward a confrontation with the ones who destroyed his home.

Near Dras-Leona the king's servants ambush the travelers. Brom is mortally wounded shielding Eragon, and before he dies he confesses that he too was once a Dragon Rider, giving Eragon his blessing. A young stranger named Murtagh appears, drives off the attackers, and joins Eragon on the road. Haunted by visions of a beautiful woman imprisoned and in pain, Eragon is drawn to the fortress city of Gil'ead, where he is captured but then breaks free, rescuing the prisoner of his dreams. She is an elf named Arya, poisoned during her long captivity and desperately needing the rebels' healers. With Murtagh and Saphira, Eragon flees the city with her, pursued and running out of time.

To save the dying Arya, Eragon, Saphira, and Murtagh make a grueling crossing of the Hadarac Desert toward the mountains, guided by Arya's fevered directions to the Varden, the rebels fighting the Empire. Murtagh, oddly, dreads reaching them and reveals little of why. They arrive at Farthen Dur, a hidden stronghold within a hollow mountain shared with the dwarves, where Arya is at last healed. Eragon meets the Varden's stern leader, Ajihad, and his sharp daughter Nasuada, is tested and questioned, and learns how precarious the alliance of humans, dwarves, and elves really is. Their respite is short: word comes that a great army of the king's monstrous Urgals is marching to destroy the stronghold.

The Urgal host attacks Farthen Dur, and a savage battle rages through the mountain's caverns and the dwarf city within it. Eragon and Saphira fight in the thick of it and come face to face with the Shade Durza, the deadliest of the king's servants. Durza gravely wounds Eragon, opening a long scar across his back, but at the decisive instant Saphira and Arya distract the Shade, and Eragon drives his blade into Durza's heart, killing him. The Shade's death shatters the enemy's coordination and the Varden win the day. As Eragon recovers from his wound, a powerful presence touches his mind: a hidden teacher called the Cripple Who Is Whole, who tells him he must come to the elves' forest to be properly trained. His first war survived, Eragon and Saphira ready themselves to leave, their role in the struggle against Galbatorix just beginning.

characters.description: The Discworld's least capable wizard, who has spent an unmeasurable stretch of time lost in the Dungeon Dimensions, the formless space outside reality where shapeless Things press against the world. He can perform no magic at all, is a coward on principle, and is pulled back into the world by a summoning meant for something far more impressive. He wants nothing more than to be somewhere safe and boring, and never is.
characters.name: Rincewind

characters.description: A teenage demonologist working out of his grandfather's cellar, self-taught from books and entirely confident that the rules he has read are the rules that apply. He summons a demon in order to claim the traditional three wishes: to rule the kingdoms of the world, to meet the most beautiful woman who ever lived, and to live forever. He is spotty, pedantic, argumentative, and completely unprepared for what any of those wishes would actually be like.
characters.name: Eric Thursley

characters.description: Eric's parrot, whose vocabulary is small, repetitive and largely obscene, and who accompanies the pair through most of their travels. It has a talent for appearing at moments when a comment is least helpful.
characters.name: Eric's parrot

characters.description: The current King of Hell, a modern demon who rose through the ranks by administration rather than by cruelty. He has reorganised the underworld away from pitchforks and fire and toward committees, safety notices, mandatory leisure activities and paperwork, on the theory that boredom is a far more efficient torment. He is enormously proud of the reforms, keeps detailed records of everything, and is quietly resented by the older demon lords, who remember how the place used to be run.
characters.name: Astfgl

characters.description: The god of the Tezuman Empire, a jungle people who invented the calendar, take a gloomy view of existence, and are thoroughly tired of the deity who demands their blood sacrifices. Their carvings describe him as part man, part chicken and part jaguar, and he requires a steady supply of hearts cut out on the temple steps, which is the chief reason his worshippers are so tired of him.
characters.name: Quezovercoatl

characters.description: An elderly and determined explorer who has spent his career searching the jungles for the Fountain of Youth, and who has got closer to it than anyone else. Talkative and unshakeably cheerful about the hardships of the trail, he crosses paths with the travellers in Tezuman country.
characters.name: Ponce da Quirm

characters.description: The woman whose abduction started the long war between Tsort and Ephebe, and who is therefore, by reputation, the most beautiful woman who ever lived. The siege has now run for a very long time. She has settled comfortably into life in the besieged city, has a large family and a great deal to do, and has no intention of being rescued by anybody.
characters.name: Elenor of Tsort

characters.description: The Ephebian strategist who devised the wooden horse and the plan to end the siege of Tsort, and who is tired, underappreciated and mainly concerned with getting home afterwards. He is a distant ancestor of Rincewind, and the resemblance in both name and temperament is not a coincidence.
characters.name: Lavaeolus

characters.description: The maker of the Discworld, encountered at the very beginning of time while the world is still being assembled. He works from a checklist, is absorbed in the details of coastlines and small creatures, and is mildly interested rather than alarmed to find two visitors present before there is anywhere for them to have come from.
characters.name: The Creator

characters.description: Rincewind's walking chest of sapient pearwood, separated from him and left to make its own way back across places that were never meant to be walked through. It arrives battered, scarred and in a worse temper than usual, and it is still entirely single-minded about finding its owner.
characters.name: The Luggage

characters.description: One of the oldest of the demon lords, from the era when Hell was run on traditional lines, and a survivor of every regime since. Courteous, ancient and extremely patient, he has watched the new management's reforms with quiet disapproval and has been waiting a long time for the right opportunity.
characters.name: Duke Vassenego

recaps.ending: In Hell, Rincewind and Eric discover that the whole sequence of wishes was arranged by Astfgl, the King of Hell, who wanted Rincewind brought within reach and used Eric's summoning to do it. Astfgl's real weakness is not the two of them but his own court: the ancient demon lords, led by Duke Vassenego, have had enough of his committees, forms and improving schemes. Rather than depose him, they promote him. Astfgl is elevated to Supreme Life President of Hell, a magnificent title with an enormous office, ceremonial honours and no authority over anything at all, and the old lords quietly take the running of the underworld back into their own hands. With Astfgl neutralised, the new management has no further interest in the pair and sends them home. The Luggage, which has crossed the Dungeon Dimensions and Hell itself to reach its owner, is reunited with Rincewind. Eric returns to his grandfather's cellar with his three wishes technically granted and thoroughly regretted, and Rincewind is back on the Discworld, alive, unimproved, and once again in possession of a piece of luggage he did not ask for.
recaps.in_short: Rincewind, lost in the Dungeon Dimensions, is hauled back into the world by Eric Thursley, a teenage demonologist who has summoned what he believes is a demon and demands the traditional three wishes: to rule the world, to meet the most beautiful woman who ever lived, and to live forever. To Rincewind's alarm the wishes work. The first drops them in the Tezuman Empire, where Rincewind is briefly worshipped as a god and the actual god, Quezovercoatl, comes to a sudden end. The second takes them to the siege of Tsort, where the legendary Elenor turns out to be middle-aged, contented and uninterested in rescue, and where the strategist Lavaeolus, an ancestor of Rincewind, ends the war with a wooden horse. The third puts them at the beginning of time, watching the Creator assemble the Discworld, which is what living forever actually means. The wishes were engineered by Astfgl, King of Hell, who has turned the underworld into a bureaucracy of tedium. In Hell the old demon lords remove Astfgl by promoting him to a grand and powerless title, and the pair are sent home, with the Luggage.

recaps.text: Previously: Rincewind is a wizard of Ankh-Morpork's Unseen University who cannot cast a single spell, having had one of the eight great spells of the Octavo lodged in his head for most of his life. He survived a long series of catastrophes as guide to the tourist Twoflower, and inherited from him the Luggage, a walking chest of sapient pearwood that is devoted to its owner and murderous to everyone else. When raw sourcery returned to the Disc and the wizards nearly destroyed the world, Rincewind ended the crisis by staying to hold the line and was left stranded outside reality, in the Dungeon Dimensions, where shapeless Things drift and time is not a useful idea. He has been there ever since, and this book opens with him still in it.

Eric Thursley, a teenage demonologist working from his grandfather's cellar, performs a summoning and gets Rincewind, dragged out of the Dungeon Dimensions by a spell aimed at something far more impressive. Eric refuses to accept that he has not conjured a demon and demands the three wishes he is owed: to be ruler of the kingdoms of the world, to meet the most beautiful woman who ever lived, and to live forever. Rincewind protests that he can do nothing whatsoever, snaps his fingers to prove it, and the world obligingly changes around them. The first wish deposits the pair, with Eric's foul-mouthed parrot, in the jungle empire of the Tezumen, a gloomy people who invented the calendar and are dominated by a god who demands a great deal of blood. Rincewind is taken for a ruler sent from elsewhere, which is initially better than the alternative and rapidly stops being so.

The Tezumen prepare to sacrifice Rincewind and Eric, having concluded that this is what one does with visitors. They also make it clear that they thoroughly resent their own god, whose demands have made their lives miserable for generations. Quezovercoatl himself is summoned to the ceremony, and the carvings turn out to have left out the single most important fact about him: he is about six inches tall. He is stepped on almost immediately, and the Tezumen, freed of him, take the whole matter rather well. In the same stretch of jungle the travellers encounter Ponce da Quirm, an elderly explorer who has spent his life hunting for the Fountain of Youth and believes he is close to it. Eric, meanwhile, is dissatisfied: ruling the world is not what he imagined, and he wants to move on to his second wish.

The second wish carries them to the long siege of Tsort, the war fought over the abduction of Elenor, whose beauty is supposed to be the greatest the world has known. By the time they arrive the siege has been running for years, and Elenor is a comfortable, busy woman with a large family who regards the whole war as an inconvenience and has no wish to be rescued. Rincewind and Eric fall in with the Ephebian side and end up inside the great wooden horse, the plan of the strategist Lavaeolus, a weary and undervalued tactician who wants chiefly to finish the job and go home, and who is an ancestor of Rincewind in both name and outlook. The horse works, Tsort falls, and Eric, having met the most beautiful woman who ever lived and found her entirely unlike the story, moves on to his third wish.

The third wish, to live forever, is granted from the correct end: the pair are set down at the very beginning of time, where the Creator is still assembling the Discworld from a checklist and has not yet finished the coastlines. Eric grasps that living forever includes all the time before anything happens, which is most of it and is extremely dull. They get away from the dawn of the world, but the wishes have not been coming from nowhere. Every one of them has been routed through Hell, and the pair are delivered there, into an underworld that has been comprehensively modernised: no pitchforks, no flames, but queues, forms, safety regulations, compulsory recreation and improving lectures, all instituted by its current king. Rincewind's Luggage, meanwhile, has been making its own way across the Dungeon Dimensions in search of him, and it is not in a good mood.

Astfgl, King of Hell, reveals that Eric's summoning was his own work and that the entire tour of wishes was a device to get Rincewind where he wanted him. But his position is weaker than he thinks. The ancient demon lords have endured his reforms for as long as they intend to, and Duke Vassenego, oldest of them, springs the trap he has been preparing: Astfgl is publicly elevated to Supreme Life President of Hell, a title of enormous dignity, a vast office, ceremonial precedence and no power over anything whatsoever. The old lords resume control of the underworld, drop their interest in the two visitors, and send them home. The Luggage catches up with Rincewind at last, battered by its journey. Eric is returned to his grandfather's cellar with all three wishes granted and none of them wanted, and Rincewind is back on the Discworld, no better off than before but a great deal better off than he was in the Dungeon Dimensions.
